gallery.title: File:Sunshine State (52539944919).jpg
gallery.description: A view from "Manatee Sanctuary Park" in Cape Canaveral, FL, looking out over the Banana River. We were staying just to the south in Cocoa Beach, visiting the Space Coast to watch the rocket launch of Artemis I from Kennedy Space Center. After a lunch at "Zachary's" we went down the street to this little community park that offered a quite pleasant place to stroll around.

gallery.filename: Kennedy Space Center View of Artemis I (52492673149).jpg
gallery.title: File:Kennedy Space Center View of Artemis I (52492673149).jpg
gallery.description:
A look across Banana Creek outside the Appolo/Saturn V Center at NASA Kennedy Space Center in Florida. On the left side of the photo you can see the Space Launch System (SLS) with the Orion spacecraft on pad 39B, performing testing for the Artemis I mission.

This was from a visit to KSC on 20 March 2022, just a few days after the roll out from the VAB for a wet dress rehearsal. It was later rolled back into the VAB, back out, back in, back out for launch, back in for a hurricane, and back out again. We're hoping to be back on Merrit Island in Florida next week to see Artemis launch to the moon.

gallery.filename: Cape Canaveral, Kennedy Space Center, Florida (sl2-106-1194).jpg
gallery.title: File:Cape Canaveral, Kennedy Space Center, Florida (sl2-106-1194).jpg
gallery.description: SL2-106-1194 (22 June 1973) --- This overhead view of the central eastern shore of Florida shows the Cape Canaveral and Kennedy Space Center (28.5N, 80.5W), where all of the NASA manned space missions originate. Sprinkled along the jutting cape are a number of KSC launch pads from the earlier Mercury, Gemini Apollo and Skylab series of spaceflights. Merritt Island, just south of Kennedy Space Center, is where the spacecraft liftoff tracking station is located. Photo credit: NASA

hero.title: File:Cape canaveral.jpg
hero.credit: Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth (image link)
hero.description: Cape Canaveral, Florida and the NASA John F. Kennedy Space Center are shown in this near-vertical photograph. Numerous launch pads line the Atlantic Ocean coast near the center of the photograph. To the north of the multiple launch pads, the Space Shuttle landing runway, the Shuttle Assembly Area, and Shuttle Launch Pads A and B are visible. To the south of the multiple launch pads are Port Canaveral and the city of Cocoa Beach, Florida. To the west of the space complex, five causeways span the Indian and Banana Rivers. Interstate Highway 95 is the main artery traversing south to north just west of the Florida cities of Cocoa and Titusville.
